chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tathari said: My father Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ali ibn Abi Shu'ba al-Halabi narrated from his father, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah), then he died, what is her waiting period ('iddah)? He said: Fifty-six days. It is understood that this refers to if the wife was a slave-girl owned by a group of people, and the man enjoyed her with their permission, so her waiting period is the waiting period of slave-girls, fifty-six days, as we have previously established, if she was not a mother of children.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman in temporary marriage if her husband dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies that the 'iddah for a woman in a temporary marriage (mut'ah) upon her husband's death is fifty-six days and nights, aligning with the ruling for slave-girls. The scholar notes this applies specifically if she is not a mother of children, distinguishing it from the longer waiting period for free women who bear children, reflecting the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the status of the wife in mut'ah.
